about: The 30 hardest sites we know of, which staging's live-site check (.github/workflows/bank.yml) reads every night on staging, and by hand (UNB-249; on every push too until 21 Nov 2026, UNB-166; Lewis, 20 Nov 2026: "staging focuses on the top 30 hardest sites"). Each case is a run_bank.py case (site, goal, url with {q}, three values) and carries `hard`: the wall or the trouble, the evidence that it is hard, and what a right answer holds. run_bank.py's rule reads each answer; hard_sites.py sorts each site into right, wrong, needs a browser, walled or unknown. Built 20 Nov 2026 from the hard-site ledger (hard-sites.json and the memory ledger it was copied from), the nightly Lundy bank runs of 15-20 Nov, the nightly full task gate of 20 Nov and the hard-site tickets. A site leaves only with a reason, written in left_out.

check: Every site is asked five times by run_bank.py on a fresh scratch node: `first` (values[0], the node learns), `replay` (values[1] through the learned route), `call_unrelated` (values[2]), `no_results` (a nonsense word: the answer must hold no results) and `recheck` (values[0] again: the same answer). Each answer must mention its own value in lines no other answer shares; `expect: ["price"]` also needs 3 or more prices. The site is right only when all five pass and no warm call needed the node's browser.

left_out.why: Needs a signed-in X account (ledger 11 Nov 2026: signed-out search redirects to /i/jf/onboarding/web); a scratch node in CI has none, so it would only ever say walled.
Sign-in and form writes, not public reads; the ledger's evidence is for writes a scratch node must not make.
A blog with no search to vary (ledger 12 Nov 2026: Vercel Security Checkpoint); run_bank.py needs a {q} the answer changes with.

Regressed with wrong answers on the same cause as accuweather.com (UNB-244: a second value makes the node walk again); accuweather.com stands for the class here, and all four stay in the task gate's lundy:* tasks.
